Build a rain-powered light

Real-life application

Rain and sun lighting for a house in a new residential complex. Rain from the roof runs down the drainpipe through a small water wheel that makes electricity for an outdoor path light. A rooftop solar panel runs the main 3 W light, and a battery takes over only when the sun is weak.

In the model, rain fills a raised tank. The water falls onto a little wheel and spins it. The spinning wheel turns magnets past a coil of wire you wind yourself, which makes electricity to light an LED. A small solar panel powers the 3 W bulb.

How this meets the brief

Every rule from the brief's Requirements and Constraints, and how this design follows it.

  • ✓
    At least 3 stages of energy changeThe water chain has 4: potential → kinetic → mechanical → electrical → light. The solar panel adds a fifth (light → electrical).
  • ✓
    Looks like a real-life use, stated at the startSee the green box at the top of this page. Put the same sentence on your first slide.
  • ✓
    At least one renewable sourceTwo: rain (water power) and sunlight (solar).
  • ✓
    Size between 40 × 50 cm and 50 × 70 cmA 50 × 70 cm board with every part on it.
  • ✓
    Runs a 3–5 W load
  • ✓
    No bought pump, motor or fan as a stageNone are used. The generator is magnets and a coil you wind by hand.
  • ✓
    Every stage made by hand (DIY)The wheel, straw bearings, generator, tank, valve, roof and gutter are all homemade.
  • ✓
    Battery only as a backupThe solar panel charges the battery, and it only runs the bulb when the sun is weak.
  • ✓
    Only ready-made device is the renewable oneThe solar panel is the only bought device. Diodes, LEDs, wire and the battery are parts, not machines.
Confirm these with your assistant lecturer before you build:
  • That the solar panel can carry the 3 W bulb. A water wheel this size makes far less than 1 W (try the numbers below), so no water rig that fits on the board can reach 3 W alone.
  • That diodes and LEDs count as parts, not ready-made devices.
  • How they want you to measure the wheel's mechanical energy (stage 3 in the readings table).

Watch it work

This side view is drawn to scale from your numbers. The green numbered dots light up as the water moves through each stage.

Your energy stages

Each stage changes energy from one form to another. Energy is counted in joules (J), and every stage wastes some as heat, friction or splashing. That's normal for any machine, and it's the "energy conservation" idea the project is about.

2What you'll need

For the base and stand

  • A board, 50 × 70 cm (wood or thick cardboard)
  • 4 wooden sticks or dowels for posts, plus extra for the tank stand
  • Hot glue gun, strong tape, scissors or a craft knife

For the wheel and generator (all handmade)

  • 2 plastic lids or old CDs about 12 cm across
  • 8 plastic spoons or bottle caps (the blades)
  • 1 long wooden skewer (the axle) and 2 drinking straws
  • 4 small strong magnets (neodymium discs) and a 6 cm card or plastic disc
  • About 30–40 m of thin enamelled copper wire (0.2–0.3 mm), plus sandpaper

For the water

  • A plastic box or large bottle for the tank
  • A short piece of tube and a binder clip (the valve)
  • Card for the roof, half a plastic bottle for the gutter
  • A tray to catch the water, and a watering can as the "rain"

For the electrics

  • 5 diodes (1N5817 type wastes the least power): 4 for the coil, 1 for the solar panel
  • 1 small red LED for the water-wheel circuit
  • 1 LED bulb, 3 W, rated for your battery's voltage (for example 6 V)
  • 1 small solar panel, about 6 V and 5–6 W: the only ready-made device allowed
  • 1 rechargeable battery pack matching the panel's voltage (backup only)
  • Wires with crocodile clips, a multimeter, and a phone stopwatch

Sizes to build

The brief doesn't limit height, but check with your assistant lecturer if your tank needs to sit high.

3Build it, step by step

Tick each step off as you go. Your ticks are remembered on this device.

    Board plan from above

    Use this to mark where everything goes before you glue anything.

    Dashed shapes are held up above the board. The axle runs along the board's 50 cm side: wheel first, then the magnet disc, then the coil.

    Readings table (Milestone 2)

    The brief asks for at least 3 readings from each stage, their average, the deviations and the % error against your calculation. Type each run's measured energy in joules and the page does the maths. Set the numbers at the top to match your test so the calculated values line up.

    Deviation = each reading minus the average. % error = (calculated − average) ÷ calculated × 100. Your readings are remembered on this device.

    Other real-life uses

    • Small turbines inside city water pipes. Water already flowing to homes spins a turbine in the pipe and makes electricity (Portland, USA has done this).
    • Micro-hydro in hill villages. A stream is sent down a pipe to a small turbine that lights homes where there's no power grid.
    • Rainwater turbines in tall buildings. Rain falling down a high building's drainpipes can turn small generators for stair or corridor lights.

    Words explained

    Joule (J)
    A unit of energy. Lifting a 1 kg bag of sugar 10 cm uses about 1 J.
    Watt (W)
    How fast energy is used or made. Watts = joules ÷ seconds. A phone charger gives about 5 W.
    Potential energy
    Energy something has because it's high up. E = m × g × h.
    Kinetic energy
    Energy something has because it's moving. E = ½ × m × v².
    Efficiency
    The share of energy a stage passes on. 40% means 40 of every 100 J make it through.
    Axle and bearing
    The axle is the stick the wheel spins on. The bearing (here, a straw) holds it while letting it turn.
    Coil
    Wire wound round and round. When a magnet moves past it, a small electric current flows in the wire.
    Enamelled wire
    Copper wire with a thin clear coating so the turns don't touch electrically. Sand the ends to connect it.
    Diode
    A one-way valve for electricity. The stripe marks the end the current comes out of.
    Diode bridge
    4 diodes arranged so the back-and-forth current from the coil always comes out flowing one way.
    Ammeter / voltmeter
    Both are settings on a multimeter. Ammeter measures current (amps) and goes in the loop of wire. Voltmeter measures voltage (volts) and goes across a part.
    Deviation and % error
    Deviation shows how far each reading is from your average. % error shows how far your average is from what the equations predict.
    For the curious: change the efficiency guesses

    Each stage passes on only part of its energy. These are starting guesses in %. Once you test your own parts you can replace them.

    The maths: starting energy E = m × g × h (mass in kg, g = 9.81, height in m), and 1 L of water weighs 1 kg. The outlet size comes from flow rate = 0.6 × hole area × √(2 × g × h).
